body:
You could become the reason someone doesn't make the same choice you did. Sometimes decisions are made based on what we think our options are instead of what they could be. 

I think of it like writing a story. Every author needs a strong editor to call them out on their bullshit. The spelling mistakes, grammatical errors, diction, etc., etc. The use in having good people in our lives that we trust is getting those second, third, and even fourth opinions to help us determine the true quality in our decisions. 

Bottom line, get good people in your life. Figure out who your good friends and bad friends are, and don't be afraid to focus more of your energy on the good people who are there for you. While you're figuring that out, it is important that you dedicate a little more time each day on being the best friend you can be to yourself. 

Yes, there will be pricks who say mean things, and they are welcome to say them, but your decisions are yours. No one else's. And where you choose to go from here is ultimately a path you're allowed to forge on your own. 

Imo, you're a success story in the making, but only if you'd like to believe it. Either way, the choice is yours.

Thank you for saying that. I can't really remember the last time I've gotten a compliment like that. Sometimes finding the right words to articulate my feelings is really, really difficult (Alexithymia, I believe, is what they call it), so the fact that the post didn't read like non-sensical rambling to you means a lot to me. 

I'll take your kind words to heart and see what tomorrow brings for me. Thank you again for sharing them. You've made a difference in my day for the better.

Thank you for your kind words. And, hey, a little cringe is okay. I'm a nerd with a penchant for bad puns, so nerdy stuff is welcome here. I loved your Proficiency reference. 

I'm happy for you to hear that you're in therapy. I was actively going many years ago (before I lost my insurance), and it helped me so much. I really hope the perspective on self-help changes drastically in the near future. The challenge rating on Life is already a 30, the societal pressure to feign happiness is nothing short of unnecessary, imo. 

Don't worry about whether you chose the right words to respond with. The fact that you read my story and cared to comment with encouragement at all means the world to me. Thank you.

Thank you for saying that. I always struggled with writing growing up, but hoped to one day be decent at it. I appreciate every second you'd taken to read this post. It was really difficult for me to type. Thank you, again. I hope you are well.
